title: Sidecar transport profiles: client-side socket warming, lease hints, and streaming backpressure examples
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Problem: SDKs for Python/TypeScript/Go need ergonomic cross-language guidance and runtime support for high-throughput LLM inference. Applications see tail latency from cold connections, head-of-line blocking in multiplexed transports, and poor streaming UX when a single slow connection stalls progress. Objective: design and ship a set of "sidecar transport profiles" and SDK primitives that enable: (1) client-side socket warming (proactive TCP/GPU path priming), (2) per-route lease hints and light-weight connection pooling, (3) adaptive keep-alive tuning by runtime heuristics, and (4) streaming backpressure/hedging examples and recipes across Python/TS/Go. Deliverables: - Sidecar profile specification (JSON schema) for per-route connection hints and warmup policies. - Reference SDK changes and example recipes for Python, TypeScript, Go showing how to opt-in to sidecar profiles and safe defaults. - Benchmarks (p95/p99 latency, throughput, and CPU) and a test harness with simulated slow endpoints. - Gradual rollout plan and telemetry/alerting signals to detect regressions.
acceptance_criteria: Sidecar transport profile schema published in repo and documented in SDK docs
Python/TS/Go SDKs include helpers to load a transport profile and apply it at client creation
End-to-end benchmark shows >20% reduction in p99 for cold-start-heavy workloads with socket warming enabled
Streaming tests demonstrate graceful progress when one connection in a pool stalls (no full stall of all streams)
Automated tests for profile parsing and safety checks added to CI
implementation_notes: High level design: introduce a minimal sidecar-profile JSON that callers (or platform sidecars) can provide to each SDK client. The profile will include: - connection_pool: {min_connections, max_connections, lease_timeout_ms, per_route_cap} - warmup: {enable, parallel_probes, probe_payload_type} - keepalive: {tcp_keepalive_ms, probe_interval_ms, retry_limit} - streaming: {per_stream_window_tokens, backpressure_strategy:(pause|hedge|drain), hedge_delay_ms} SDK change strategy: - Add a TransportProfile loader in each SDK that merges server-side defaults, sidecar profile, and app overrides. - Implement non-blocking warmup probes that establish TCP+TLS and send tiny priming requests (no cost). - Expose an API for callers to hint request priority and route tags so sidecar can preferentially warm certain paths. - Backpressure: implement a token-window per-stream and soft-hedging: if a stream makes no progress for hedge_delay_ms, open a speculative request on a different connection and cancel the slower one on first successful token batch. Safety and cost controls: warmup probes should be disabled for users with low-usage accounts and capped at a configurable rate. Provide telemetry hooks for warmup success/failure, hedge occurrences, and connection churn. Cross-language ergonomics: provide identical function names and semantics (TransportProfile.from_json, client.with_transport_profile(profile), client.set_priority_hint("routing.key")) across SDKs. Examples will be idiomatic per language (async/await Python/TS, context-managed Go).
progress_updates: 2026-03-02: Spike complete for warmup probe mechanism in Go client. Proof-of-concept establishes TCP+TLS then issues an empty /health POST; reduces first-request latency in local harness.
2026-03-03: Design review with runtime team. Decided warmup probes must avoid model inference cost (use lightweight path). Need sidecar to expose /priming endpoint that returns a 204 when primed.
2026-03-04: Began Python SDK hooks (TransportProfile loader + merge). Added unit tests for parsing invalid lease_timeout values.
2026-03-05: Draft sidecar-profile schema pushed to repo (WIP). Opening RFC PR for cross-sdk API names and telemetry keys.
